row.question:
Based on the chest X-ray findings (Figure 1) and using the available diagnostic tools, which of the following is the most likely explanation for the observed hyperlucency and reduced size of the left lung in this patient?

A) Technical issues such as patient rotation causing uneven radiographic exposure
B) Mastectomy on the left side resulting in thoracic wall changes
C) Pneumothorax leading to a hyperlucent lung appearance
D) Emphysema causing hyperinflation of the left lung
E) Swyer-James-McLeod syndrome characterized by a smaller, hyperlucent lung with reduced vascular markings
F) Pleural effusion on the right side causing compensatory hyperlucency of the left lung

reference.correct_choice_text: Swyer-James-McLeod syndrome characterized by a smaller, hyperlucent lung with reduced vascular markings

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When CXR shows unilateral lung hyperlucency with reduced vascular markings and small hilum, but side assignment is ambiguous due to rotation or mediastinal shift
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect rib spacing and diaphragm position: reduced intercostal space + elevated hemidiaphragm on the same side confirms volume loss (not hyperinflation); correlate with hilum size and vascular tapering
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable in severe scoliosis or if diaphragm obscured by gastric air; requires adequate inspiration

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When mediastinal opacity obscures one heart border and tracheal deviation is present on PA CXR
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect which cardiac border is silhouetted (left border loss = left mediastinal pathology; right border loss = right-sided) and confirm tracheal deviation direction—deviation away from mass side—and compare costophrenic angle blunting severity per side.
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable if both borders obscured or in severe cardiomegaly; requires adequate inspiration and centering.
